title: Polynomial bound test is polynomial-time computable
statement: For any natural numbers $C$ and $c$, the function that sends a bit string $z$ to the one-bit string indicating whether its decoded pair $(a,b)$ satisfies $|b|\le C(|a|+1)^c$ is polynomial-time computable; strings that do not decode as pairs are assigned indicator value $0$.
replaced:
For $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\beta_{C,c}(z)$, for a binary string $z$, be the
bit $1$ if $z = \langle a, b\rangle$ is a well-formed self-delimiting pair encoding
($a$ with every bit doubled, then $01$, then $b$) with $|b| \le C(|a|+1)^c$, and
the bit $0$ otherwise. Then for all $C, c \in \mathbb{N}$ the map sending $z$ to
the one-bit string $\beta_{C,c}(z)$ is polynomial-time computable: some finite
multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet computes it within
$D(n+1)^d$ steps on every input of length $n$, for some constants
$D, d \in \mathbb{N}$.
